_what: M3 held-out reference labels, competitor half. 40 TikTok publications from 33 competitor creators, none in the 24-video tuning set.
_labelled_by: Claude (Opus 5), from four-frame strips at t=0,1,2,3s, 2026-10-27.
_ordering_disclosure: Labelled BEFORE any inference was run against these 40. No model or detector output was consulted. Strips were generated by scripts/provision/make_holdout_strips.py --kind competitor.
_spent_by: SPENT, 2026-10-27, by M3. These labels have now been used to make a model-selection decision: they promoted `vision_face_visible`, confirmed `vision_text_overlay_present`, and rejected the negative-example prompt. A set used to select can no longer measure generalisation of what it selected - which is exactly what happened to the 24 labels in human_labels_v2.json, twice. The original benchmark stays as it is and these figures must not be restated as fresh evidence for the thing they chose. Any future model-selection decision needs a NEW prospective holdout, labelled before that model's output exists. Tracked in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md section 11.
_the_frames_are_gone: ADR 0009. The mp4s and the strips these labels came from lived in the quarantine directory under a six-hour TTL and have been deleted. The labels are derived data and persist; the media did not. Re-checking a label means re-acquiring that publication, which costs about $0.004 per file (measured 2026-10-27: 40 files for $0.1616).
_why_this_half_matters_more: The own-account half has no negatives at all for performer_visible and only one for text_overlay_present, so those fields cannot be measured there. This half has 5 and 11. It is also the only unseen-creator evidence in M3: 40 publications from 33 different creators, none of them the owner. 33 rather than 40 because the competitor corpus holds only 48 TikTok publications across 38 creators, so a 40-video sample cannot be one per creator; seven creators contribute two.
_rule: A field is true if the thing is visible in ANY of the four frames - the same hook-window rule as holdout_labels_own.json and human_labels_v2.json, so the three sets stay comparable.

_definitions.performer_visible: Any part of a person performing. Hands alone count. A pure animation with no human in shot is FALSE.
_definitions.piano_or_keyboard_visible: Piano keys visible. A piano body, soundboard, strings or action with no keys showing does NOT count. See _ambiguity on rendered keyboards.
_definitions.face_visible: A recognisable human face, actually present in the scene. A painted or photographed face inside the shot - a portrait, a book plate - is FALSE; see _ambiguity.
_definitions.sheet_music_visible: Printed musical notation - staves and noteheads - visible anywhere, including notation composited in as a graphic. A piano-roll animation is NOT notation. Numbers printed on keys are NOT notation.
_definitions.text_overlay_present: Text the creator added on top of the video, including a handle watermark. Printed text already in the scene is not.

_ambiguity.rendered_keyboards: Publications 692, 705 and 748 are piano-roll animations whose only keyboard is drawn, not photographed. Keys are visible, so piano_or_keyboard_visible is TRUE by the literal definition - but nothing in these clips was filmed, and a reader who assumed the field means 'a real instrument was in front of a camera' would read them wrongly. Flagged in _uncertain.
_ambiguity.faces_in_artwork: 747 shows a Renoir reproduction and 751 a painted Beethoven portrait on a tablet. Both contain painted faces. Marked FALSE on the ground that the field is about a person in the scene, which is a judgement call a model may reasonably make the other way.
_ambiguity.a_piano_with_no_keys: 697, 700 and 761 all contain a piano or a score but no visible keys - 761 shows the open soundboard from above, 700 is too distant, 697 is an orchestral score with no instrument at all. These three plus 707 are the entire negative evidence for piano_or_keyboard_visible on this half, so the specificity figure rests on four publications and is correspondingly imprecise.
_ambiguity.settings_outside_the_enum: The task's `setting` enum has no value for a railway concourse or a shopping concourse, and none for a pure animation with no place in it. Rather than force a wrong label, `setting` is OMITTED for 692, 697, 705, 707, 709, 712, 744, 745, 748 and 760, and the scorer skips any field a publication does not carry.

_owner_review._what: The owner's verdict on the labels Claude flagged as ambiguous, 2026-10-28. Reviewed at #/review/labels: own-account publications from the same frames the model saw, competitor publications from the live post because ADR 0009 had deleted the media.
_owner_review._why_labels_are_not_rewritten: `labels` above is UNCHANGED and stays the published answer key, so every benchmark already reported remains reproducible from it. These corrections are additive. Use `corrected_labels()` in server/api/labels_api.py for any NEW analysis; a benchmark that silently rewrote its own answer key would make its history unreadable.
_owner_review._what_it_found: Ten of twenty-one were wrong - but these are the twenty-one Claude itself flagged out of roughly 480 label decisions, so this is the error rate on the hardest 4%, not on the set. The self-flagging worked: it found where it was unreliable. The corrections do NOT generalise to the labels nobody flagged.
